newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong students accuse university of censorship.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong students accuse university of censorship.

text.p: Just seven weeks before Hong Kong's return to China, students at a Hong Kong university have accused their school of censorship after it blocked a fund- raising event for human rights group Amnesty International.
The Hong Kong Polytechnic University student union told the South China Morning Post newspaper their application to sell Amnesty International T-shirts to raise funds was rejected.

"An employee at the (university) estate office said the university would not permit any political organisation to hold activities on campus," union leader Kan Chak-chuen was quoting as saying in the paper's Tuesday edition.
Hong Kong, a territory of 6.4 million people, reverts to China at midnight on June 30, after 156 years of colonial rule.
Concerns have been raised that media and universities would practise political self-censorship to avoid rankling Beijing after the change of flag.
Academics have already linked a number of personnel changes at Hong Kong universities to the looming handover.

London-based Amnesty International has been critical of China's human rights record and last month expressed concern over plans by Hong Kong's future government to curb some civil liberties after the sovereignty transfer.
Kan said it was the first time they had heard of any such proscription against political organisations operating on campus.
He said the student body and London-based Amnesty, which has a regional office in Hong Kong, had staged a similar fund-raising event on campus last October.

A university spokesman denied the censorship charge. He was quoted by the newspaper as saying outside groups were not allowed to raise funds on campus, and added that the October event was regarded as a social function.
Student leaders and officials from the university were not immediately available for further comment.
